<div id="algorithm1.4.40" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="algorithm1.4.40.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> </span><span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span><span id="algorithm1.4.40.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">  </span><math id="algorithm1.m44" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(P^{\prime},R^{\prime})\leftarrow\mathsf{Debias}(P,R,\Pi)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><msup><mi mathsize="0.900em">P</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">′</mo></msup><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><msup><mi mathsize="0.900em">R</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">′</mo></msup><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em" stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝖣𝖾𝖻𝗂𝖺𝗌</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">P</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">R</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em" mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(P^{\prime},R^{\prime})\leftarrow\mathsf{Debias}(P,R,\Pi)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="algorithm1.4.40.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> ;  </span><span id="algorithm1.4.40.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">// </span><span id="algorithm1.4.40.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">remove diagram-inferable cues; rewrite reasoning trace</span>
</div>
<div id="algorithm1.4.41" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="algorithm1.4.41.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> </span><span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span><span id="algorithm1.4.41.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">  </span><math id="algorithm1.m45" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}\leftarrow\mathcal{D}\cup\{(I,P^{\prime},R^{\prime},A,C_{\mathrm{plot}})\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathsize="0.900em">𝒟</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em" stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathsize="0.900em">𝒟</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">∪</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">I</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><msup><mi mathsize="0.900em">P</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">′</mo></msup><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><msup><mi mathsize="0.900em">R</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">′</mo></msup><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">A</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">C</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">plot</mi></msub><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}\leftarrow\mathcal{D}\cup\{(I,P^{\prime},R^{\prime},A,C_{\mathrm{plot}})\}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="algorithm1.4.41.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
</span>
</div>
<div id="algorithm1.4.42" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="algorithm1.4.42.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">return</span><span id="algorithm1.4.42.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> </span><math id="algorithm1.m46" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathsize="0.900em">𝒟</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="algorithm1.4.42.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">.
</span>
</div>
</div>
</figure>
<section id="A7.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.1 </span>Coordinate Verification Mechanism</h3>

<div id="A7.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The coordinate verification stage performs numerical validation to ensure that the generated coordinates satisfy all geometric constraints declared in the problem statement. This verification is critical for maintaining consistency across symbolic structure, textual description, and visual representation.</p>
</div>
<section id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Coordinate Generation.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Given a problem statement <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math>, the Coder LLM <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{code}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>code</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{code}}</annotation></semantics></math> generates Python code that computes coordinates for all geometric entities mentioned in <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math>. The generated code must satisfy several constraints: (1) all points must have distinct coordinates to avoid degeneracy, (2) all geometric relations (e.g., perpendicularity, parallelism, collinearity) must be explicitly enforced through numerical construction, and (3) the code must be executable in a sandboxed environment without external dependencies beyond standard mathematical libraries. The code is executed to obtain a coordinate dictionary <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{X}=\{p_{i}:(x_{i},y_{i})\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{X}=\{p_{i}:(x_{i},y_{i})\}</annotation></semantics></math>, where each <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is a point label and <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x_{i},y_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x_{i},y_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> are its 2D coordinates.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Geometric Constraint Verification.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">After extracting coordinates <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐗</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{X}</annotation></semantics></math> and plotting specifications <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pi</annotation></semantics></math> from the executed meta code, we perform two types of numerical checks:</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(1) Constraint Verification</span> (<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{VerifyGeometry}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝖵𝖾𝗋𝗂𝖿𝗒𝖦𝖾𝗈𝗆𝖾𝗍𝗋𝗒</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{VerifyGeometry}</annotation></semantics></math>): For each geometric relation explicitly stated in the problem <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math>, we verify that the coordinates satisfy the corresponding numerical condition. This includes:</p>
<ul id="A7.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A7.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Length constraints</span>: For any segment <math id="A7.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="AB" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">AB</annotation></semantics></math> with declared length <math id="A7.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math>, we check that <math id="A7.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\|\mathbf{X}(A)-\mathbf{X}(B)\|-l|&lt;\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\|\mathbf{X}(A)-\mathbf{X}(B)\|-l|&lt;\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A7.I1.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon=10^{-6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon=10^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math> is a numerical tolerance.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Angle constraints</span>: For any angle <math id="A7.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\angle ABC" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∠</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\angle ABC</annotation></semantics></math> with declared measure <math id="A7.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, we compute the angle using vector dot product and verify <math id="A7.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\angle(\mathbf{X}(A),\mathbf{X}(B),\mathbf{X}(C))-\theta|&lt;\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∠</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\angle(\mathbf{X}(A),\mathbf{X}(B),\mathbf{X}(C))-\theta|&lt;\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Parallelism and perpendicularity</span>: For parallel lines <math id="A7.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="AB\parallel CD" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">AB\parallel CD</annotation></semantics></math>, we verify that the angle between direction vectors is within <math id="A7.I1.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A7.I1.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0^{\circ}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0^{\circ}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="A7.I1.i3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="180^{\circ}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>180</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">180^{\circ}</annotation></semantics></math>; for perpendicular lines <math id="A7.I1.i3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="AB\perp CD" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo>⟂</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">AB\perp CD</annotation></semantics></math>, we verify the angle is within <math id="A7.I1.i3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A7.I1.i3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="90^{\circ}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>90</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">90^{\circ}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Collinearity</span>: For collinear points <math id="A7.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A,B,C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A,B,C</annotation></semantics></math>, we verify that the area of triangle <math id="A7.I1.i4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="ABC" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">ABC</annotation></semantics></math> (computed via cross product) is within <math id="A7.I1.i4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math> of zero.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Circle constraints</span>: For a circle with center <math id="A7.I1.i5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>O</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O</annotation></semantics></math> and radius <math id="A7.I1.i5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>, or a circle passing through points <math id="A7.I1.i5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A,B,C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A,B,C</annotation></semantics></math>, we verify that all declared points on the circle satisfy <math id="A7.I1.i5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\|\mathbf{X}(p)-\mathbf{X}(O)\|-r|&lt;\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\|\mathbf{X}(p)-\mathbf{X}(O)\|-r|&lt;\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math> (or equivalent for three-point circles).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(2) Answer Verification</span> (<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{VerifyAnswer}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝖵𝖾𝗋𝗂𝖿𝗒𝖠𝗇𝗌𝗐𝖾𝗋</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{VerifyAnswer}</annotation></semantics></math>): For problems with numerical answers, we evaluate the answer quantity using the generated coordinates. Specifically, we parse the DSL expression from <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pi.\mathtt{quantities}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi>𝚚𝚞𝚊𝚗𝚝𝚒𝚝𝚒𝚎𝚜</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pi.\mathtt{quantities}</annotation></semantics></math> (e.g., <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathtt{length(A,B)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝚕𝚎𝚗𝚐𝚝𝚑</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙰</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathtt{length(A,B)}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathtt{angle(A,B,C)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝚊𝚗𝚐𝚕𝚎</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙰</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙲</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathtt{angle(A,B,C)}</annotation></semantics></math>, or more complex expressions like <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathtt{length(A,B)-length(C,D)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝚕𝚎𝚗𝚐𝚝𝚑</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙰</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>𝚕𝚎𝚗𝚐𝚝𝚑</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙲</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙳</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathtt{length(A,B)-length(C,D)}</annotation></semantics></math> for proof problems). The DSL supports geometric primitives including:</p>
<ul id="A7.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A7.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Point-based quantities: <math id="A7.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathtt{length(A,B)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝚕𝚎𝚗𝚐𝚝𝚑</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙰</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathtt{length(A,B)}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A7.I2.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathtt{angle(A,B,C)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝚊𝚗𝚐𝚕𝚎</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙰</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙲</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathtt{angle(A,B,C)}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A7.I2.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathtt{area(A,B,C,\ldots)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝚊𝚛𝚎𝚊</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙰</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙲</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathtt{area(A,B,C,\ldots)}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A7.I2.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathtt{perimeter(A,B,C,\ldots)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝚙𝚎𝚛𝚒𝚖𝚎𝚝𝚎𝚛</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙰</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙲</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathtt{perimeter(A,B,C,\ldots)}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Line-based quantities: <math id="A7.I2.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathtt{angle\_between\_lines(A,B,C,D)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝚊𝚗𝚐𝚕𝚎</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>_</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝚋𝚎𝚝𝚠𝚎𝚎𝚗</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>_</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝚕𝚒𝚗𝚎𝚜</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙰</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙲</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙳</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathtt{angle\_between\_lines(A,B,C,D)}</annotation></semantics></math> and its trigonometric variants.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Circle-based quantities: <math id="A7.I2.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathtt{radius(C1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝚛𝚊𝚍𝚒𝚞𝚜</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙲𝟷</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathtt{radius(C1)}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A7.I2.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathtt{arc\_length(C1,A,B)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝚊𝚛𝚌</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>_</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝚕𝚎𝚗𝚐𝚝𝚑</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙲𝟷</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙰</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathtt{arc\_length(C1,A,B)}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A7.I2.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathtt{sector\_area(C1,A,B)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝚜𝚎𝚌𝚝𝚘𝚛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>_</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝚊𝚛𝚎𝚊</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙲𝟷</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙰</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathtt{sector\_area(C1,A,B)}</annotation></semantics></math>, etc., where <math id="A7.I2.i3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C1</annotation></semantics></math> is a circle ID.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.2" class="ltx_p">Each DSL expression is evaluated by substituting point coordinates and circle parameters, then compared against the declared answer <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> with tolerance <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">For <span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">computation problems</span>, the DSL expression directly represents the quantity to be computed (e.g., <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathtt{length(A,B)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝚕𝚎𝚗𝚐𝚝𝚑</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙰</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathtt{length(A,B)}</annotation></semantics></math> for finding the length of segment <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="AB" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">AB</annotation></semantics></math>), and we verify that the evaluated value matches the declared answer <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">For <span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">proof problems</span>, we transform the statement to be proved into a zero-value expression for numerical verification. Specifically, if the conclusion to be proved is an equality relation (e.g., “<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="AB=CD" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">AB=CD</annotation></semantics></math>”, “<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\angle ABC=\angle DEF" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∠</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∠</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>E</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>F</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\angle ABC=\angle DEF</annotation></semantics></math>”, or “<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="AB\parallel CD" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">AB\parallel CD</annotation></semantics></math>”), we convert it into a difference expression that should evaluate to zero:</p>
<ul id="A7.I3" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A7.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Equality of lengths: “<math id="A7.I3.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="AB=CD" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">AB=CD</annotation></semantics></math>” <math id="A7.I3.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A7.I3.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathtt{length(A,B)-length(C,D)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝚕𝚎𝚗𝚐𝚝𝚑</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙰</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>𝚕𝚎𝚗𝚐𝚝𝚑</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙲</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙳</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathtt{length(A,B)-length(C,D)}</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Equality of angles: “<math id="A7.I3.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\angle ABC=\angle DEF" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∠</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∠</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>E</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>F</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\angle ABC=\angle DEF</annotation></semantics></math>” <math id="A7.I3.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A7.I3.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathtt{angle(A,B,C)-angle(D,E,F)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝚊𝚗𝚐𝚕𝚎</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙰</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙲</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>𝚊𝚗𝚐𝚕𝚎</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙳</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙴</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙵</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathtt{angle(A,B,C)-angle(D,E,F)}</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I3.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I3.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I3.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Parallelism: “<math id="A7.I3.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="AB\parallel CD" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">AB\parallel CD</annotation></semantics></math>” <math id="A7.I3.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A7.I3.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathtt{angle\_between\_lines(A,B,C,D)-0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝚊𝚗𝚐𝚕𝚎</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>_</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝚋𝚎𝚝𝚠𝚎𝚎𝚗</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>_</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝚕𝚒𝚗𝚎𝚜</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙰</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙲</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙳</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>𝟶</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathtt{angle\_between\_lines(A,B,C,D)-0}</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I3.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I3.i4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I3.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Perpendicularity: “<math id="A7.I3.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="AB\perp CD" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo>⟂</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">AB\perp CD</annotation></semantics></math>” <math id="A7.I3.i4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A7.I3.i4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathtt{angle\_between\_lines(A,B,C,D)-90}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝚊𝚗𝚐𝚕𝚎</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>_</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝚋𝚎𝚝𝚠𝚎𝚎𝚗</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>_</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝚕𝚒𝚗𝚎𝚜</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙰</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙲</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙳</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>𝟿𝟶</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathtt{angle\_between\_lines(A,B,C,D)-90}</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I3.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I3.i5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I3.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Collinearity: “Points <math id="A7.I3.i5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A,B,C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A,B,C</annotation></semantics></math> are collinear” <math id="A7.I3.i5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A7.I3.i5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathtt{area(A,B,C)-0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝚊𝚛𝚎𝚊</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙰</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙲</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>𝟶</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathtt{area(A,B,C)-0}</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I3.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I3.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.I3.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Ratio relations: “<math id="A7.I3.i6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="AB:CD=EF:GH" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>F</mi></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">AB:CD=EF:GH</annotation></semantics></math>” <math id="A7.I3.i6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A7.I3.i6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathtt{length(A,B)/length(C,D)-length(E,F)/length(G,H)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>𝚕𝚎𝚗𝚐𝚝𝚑</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙰</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>𝚕𝚎𝚗𝚐𝚝𝚑</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙲</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙳</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>𝚕𝚎𝚗𝚐𝚝𝚑</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙴</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙵</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>𝚕𝚎𝚗𝚐𝚝𝚑</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝙶</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝙷</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathtt{length(A,B)/length(C,D)-length(E,F)/length(G,H)}</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.2" class="ltx_p">We then evaluate the transformed expression using the generated coordinates and verify that the result is within <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math> of zero, confirming that the geometric relation holds numerically. This zero-value verification approach enables rigorous validation of proof statements through coordinate-based computation, ensuring that the symbolic conclusion is consistent with the numerical instantiation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Annotation Consistency Check.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Beyond constraint and answer verification, we also validate that annotations in <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pi.\mathtt{annotations}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi>𝚊𝚗𝚗𝚘𝚝𝚊𝚝𝚒𝚘𝚗𝚜</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pi.\mathtt{annotations}</annotation></semantics></math> are consistent with the computed coordinates:</p>
<ul id="A7.I4" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A7.I4.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I4.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I4.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I4.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Length annotations</span>: For each entry <math id="A7.I4.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext='[["A","B"],v]' display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>"</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>"</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>"</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>"</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[["A","B"],v]</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="A7.I4.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathtt{length\_of\_line}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝚕𝚎𝚗𝚐𝚝𝚑</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>_</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝚘𝚏</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>_</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝚕𝚒𝚗𝚎</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathtt{length\_of\_line}</annotation></semantics></math>, we verify that the actual length <math id="A7.I4.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{X}(A)-\mathbf{X}(B)\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{X}(A)-\mathbf{X}(B)\|</annotation></semantics></math> matches the annotated value <math id="A7.I4.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>v</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> (after parsing LaTeX expressions like <math id="A7.I4.i1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\sqrt{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I4.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I4.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I4.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I4.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Right angle annotations</span>: For each entry <math id="A7.I4.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext='["A","B","C"]' display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>"</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>"</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>"</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>"</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>"</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>"</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">["A","B","C"]</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="A7.I4.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathtt{right\_angles}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝚛𝚒𝚐𝚑𝚝</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>_</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝚊𝚗𝚐𝚕𝚎𝚜</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathtt{right\_angles}</annotation></semantics></math>, we verify that <math id="A7.I4.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\angle(\mathbf{X}(A),\mathbf{X}(B),\mathbf{X}(C))=90^{\circ}\pm\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∠</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mn>90</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup><mo>±</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\angle(\mathbf{X}(A),\mathbf{X}(B),\mathbf{X}(C))=90^{\circ}\pm\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I4.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I4.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.I4.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I4.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Angle measure annotations</span>: For each entry <math id="A7.I4.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext='[["A","B","C"],\theta]' display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>"</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>"</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>"</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>"</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>"</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>"</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[["A","B","C"],\theta]</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="A7.I4.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathtt{measure\_of\_angle}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝚖𝚎𝚊𝚜𝚞𝚛𝚎</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>_</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝚘𝚏</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>_</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝚊𝚗𝚐𝚕𝚎</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathtt{measure\_of\_angle}</annotation></semantics></math>, we verify that the computed angle matches <math id="A7.I4.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> (with appropriate unit conversion if the annotation uses radians).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Samples that fail any of these verification steps are discarded, ensuring that all retained instances maintain strict numerical consistency between symbolic constraints, coordinate realizations, and visual diagrams. This multi-level validation mechanism is essential for generating high-quality geometry problems with guaranteed mathematical correctness.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.2 </span>Plotting Code Format Specification</h3>

<div id="A7.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">After coordinate verification, the geometric construction is serialized into a structured <span id="A7.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">plotting code</span> format that serves as the interface between coordinate computation and diagram rendering. This format is designed to be both human-readable and machine-executable, enabling deterministic visualization while preserving all geometric information necessary for verification and reasoning.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The plotting code is represented as a JSON-like dictionary structure with the following schema:</p>
</div>
<section id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Point Coordinates.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The <span id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">points</span> field maps point labels to 2D coordinates:</p><pre id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">
"points": {
    "A": (xA, yA),
    "B": (xB, yB),
    ...
}
</pre>
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Each coordinate pair <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x_{i},y_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x_{i},y_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> must be a tuple or list of two numeric values (integers or floats). All points must have distinct coordinates to avoid degeneracy.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Segments.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The <span id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">segments</span> field lists all line segments to be drawn:</p><pre id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">
"segments": [
    ["A", "B"],
    ["B", "C"],
    ...
]
</pre>
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Each segment is represented as a two-element list containing the labels of its endpoints. Segments are drawn as straight lines connecting the specified points.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Circles.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The <span id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">circles</span> field specifies all circles in the diagram. Each circle is represented as a list with the following formats:</p>
<ul id="A7.I5" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A7.I5.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I5.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I5.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I5.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">["C1", "O", r]</span>: Circle with ID <span id="A7.I5.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">C1</span>, center at point <span id="A7.I5.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">O</span>, and radius <math id="A7.I5.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> (numeric value).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I5.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I5.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I5.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I5.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">["C2", "O", "P"]</span>: Circle with ID <span id="A7.I5.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">C2</span>, center at point <span id="A7.I5.i2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">O</span>, and radius equal to the distance from <span id="A7.I5.i2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">O</span> to <span id="A7.I5.i2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">P</span>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I5.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I5.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I5.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I5.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">["C3", "A", "B", "diameter"]</span>: Circle with ID <span id="A7.I5.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">C3</span>, where segment <span id="A7.I5.i3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">AB</span> is the diameter.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I5.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I5.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.I5.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I5.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">["C4", "A", "B", "C"]</span>: Circle with ID <span id="A7.I5.i4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">C4</span> passing through three points <span id="A7.I5.i4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">A</span>, <span id="A7.I5.i4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">B</span>, and <span id="A7.I5.i4.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">C</span>.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Each circle must have a unique ID (e.g., <span id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">C1</span>, <span id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">C2</span>, <span id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">C3</span>) that is used for referencing in DSL expressions. The circle ID is distinct from point labels and is required for all circle-related geometric quantities.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In the practical implementation of our code-based alignment, we simplify the regression target for circular entities. Although our data generation pipeline supports multiple construction methods for circles (e.g., via diameter or three points), we unify these into a standard center-radius format, specifically <span id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">["O", r]</span>, during the model training phase. As illustrated in Figure  <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ Diagram Rendering. ‣ 3.1.3 Visualization ‣ 3.1 Generation Pipeline ‣ 3 Method ‣ Synthesizing Multimodal Geometry Datasets from Scratch and Enabling Visual Alignment via Plotting Code" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, regardless of the initial construction logic, the rendering engine eventually computes a deterministic coordinate-level radius to plot the diagram. To improve the stability of structural prediction, we only require the model to regress the integer part of the radius. This design choice effectively reduces the complexity of numerical prediction while preserving the essential geometric structure required for subsequent reasoning.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Annotations.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The <span id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">annotations</span> field contains visual markers and measurements that are explicitly stated in the problem:</p><pre id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.2" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">
"annotations": {
    "right_angles": [
        ["A", "B", "C"],
        ...
    ],
    "length_of_line": [
        [["A", "B"], "5"],
        [["C", "D"], "2*sqrt(3)"],
        ...
    ],
    "measure_of_angle": [
        [["A", "B", "C"], "30"],
        ...
    ]
}
</pre>
<ul id="A7.I6" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A7.I6.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I6.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I6.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I6.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">right_angles</span>: List of angle triples <span id="A7.I6.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">["A", "B", "C"]</span> where <math id="A7.I6.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\angle ABC=90^{\circ}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∠</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>90</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\angle ABC=90^{\circ}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I6.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I6.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I6.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I6.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">length_of_line</span>: List of pairs <span id="A7.I6.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">[[segment], value]</span> where the segment (two-point list) has the specified length. The value can be a numeric string (e.g., <span id="A7.I6.i2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"5"</span>) or an expression (e.g., <span id="A7.I6.i2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"2*sqrt(3)"</span>).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I6.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I6.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.I6.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I6.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">measure_of_angle</span>: List of pairs <span id="A7.I6.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">[[angle_triple], value]</span> where the angle (three-point list) has the specified measure in degrees. The value can be a numeric string (e.g., <span id="A7.I6.i3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"30"</span>) or a radian expression with <math id="A7.I6.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> (e.g., <span id="A7.I6.i3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"pi/6"</span>).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.3" class="ltx_p">All annotations must correspond to geometric relations that are <span id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">explicitly stated</span> in the problem text, not inferred through reasoning.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Quantities.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The <span id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">quantities</span> field contains DSL expressions representing the quantities to be computed or verified:</p><pre id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.2" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">
"quantities": [
    "length(A, B)",
    "angle(A, B, C)",
    "length(A, B) - length(C, D)",
    ...
]
</pre>
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.3" class="ltx_p">For computation problems, each expression directly represents a quantity to be found. For proof problems, expressions take the form <span id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">left - right</span> (e.g., <span id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"length(A, B) - length(C, D)"</span>), which should evaluate to zero if the statement is true.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The complete plotting code structure enables deterministic rendering: given the same plotting code, the renderer produces identical diagrams. This property is crucial for maintaining consistency between the generated problem statement, the underlying geometric structure, and the visual representation, and enables plotting code to serve as an explicit supervision target for visual–symbolic alignment.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.3 </span>Seed Generation</h3>

<div id="A7.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our seed generation process leverages GenesisGeo <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite>, an improved implementation of AlphaGeometry and NewClid <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>]</cite>, to construct symbolic geometric structures. To ensure consistency and compatibility with the underlying reasoning system, we maintain the same rule set used by GenesisGeo. These rules form the foundation of our symbolic reasoning engine and enable the construction of dependency graphs from predicate sets.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The rule set we employ is identical to that used in GenesisGeo, ensuring that our generated seeds are compatible with the solver’s reasoning capabilities. These rules encode fundamental geometric relationships and theorems, allowing the system to perform forward symbolic reasoning and construct proof dependency graphs. By using the same rule set, we ensure that the symbolic structures generated in our pipeline are directly compatible with GenesisGeo’s reasoning engine, enabling seamless integration between seed generation and validation.</p>
</div>
<section id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">

</div>
<div id="lstnumberx8" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">eqangle</span><span id="lstnumberx8.2" ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">P</span><span id="lstnumberx8.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx8.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">Q</span><span id="lstnumberx8.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;"> </span><span <section id="A8" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix H </span>API Usage</h2>

<div id="A8.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In section <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Effectiveness on Test-mini and Public Benchmarks ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Synthesizing Multimodal Geometry Datasets from Scratch and Enabling Visual Alignment via Plotting Code" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>, we evaluated the difficulty of our generated problems using closed-source large language model APIs. Specifically, we accessed Google’s Gemini-2.5-Pro and OpenAI’s GPT-5 through the OpenRouter API, while Qwen3-VL-32B-Thinking was served locally. Throughout the evaluation process, we ensured that both the system prompt and user prompt remained consistent across all models to guarantee fair and correct assessment.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A9" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix I </span>Limitations</h2>

<div id="A9.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Although our method successfully synthesizes geometric data, it still has several limitations.</p>
</div>
<section id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Dependence on LLM Reasoning Capabilities.</h5>

<div id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">First, during instantiation, our approach heavily relies on the reasoning capabilities of existing LLMs. We use GPT-OSS-120B as the reasoning model, and approximately 50% of samples are discarded during this process. We believe that using stronger reasoning models in the future can improve this efficiency. Additionally, methods relying on LLMs inevitably face hallucination issues, and validating their results requires additional computational overhead.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Model-Specific Evaluation.</h5>

<div id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Second, our experiments are primarily conducted on the Qwen series of models, such as Qwen2.5VL and Qwen3VL. While our approach can theoretically be directly transferred to other VLM backbones, we have not extensively validated this transferability. We also look forward to our data being used for training other series of VLMs.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Geometric Scope and Visual Style.</h5>

<div id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, our constructed geometry is limited to planar Euclidean geometry. This limitation stems from the structural foundation generated during the Seed Generation stage, which is inherently planar. Our work does not cover higher-dimensional geometric types, which represents a direction for future research. Additionally, the images we generate are idealized and presented in a textbook style, and therefore do not cover handwritten, sketch, or real exam paper styles.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A10" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix J </span>Prompts</h2>

<div id="A10.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent ltx_align_center"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A10.p1.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="549.39" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 653.15 549.39" width="653.15"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,549.39) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#CCCCCC;" fill="#CCCCCC" fill-opacity="0.5" stroke-opacity="0.5"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 3.54 3.76 L 3.54 538.55 C 3.54 542.58 6.81 545.85 10.85 545.85 L 649.39 545.85 C 653.42 545.85 656.69 542.58 656.69 538.55 L 656.69 3.76 C 656.69 -0.27 653.42 -3.54 649.39 -3.54 L 10.85 -3.54 C 6.81 -3.54 3.54 -0.27 3.54 3.76 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000099;" fill="#000099" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 5.53 L 0 543.86 C 0 546.92 2.48 549.39 5.53 549.39 L 647.61 549.39 C 650.67 549.39 653.15 546.92 653.15 543.86 L 653.15 5.53 C 653.15 2.48 650.67 0 647.61 0 L 5.53 0 C 2.48 0 0 2.48 0 5.53 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#F7F7FF;" fill="#F7F7FF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.38 5.53 L 1.38 522.15 L 651.77 522.15 L 651.77 5.53 C 651.77 3.24 649.91 1.38 647.61 1.38 L 5.53 1.38 C 3.24 1.38 1.38 3.24 1.38 5.53 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 19.16 531.62)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:32.91em;--ltx-fo-height:0.9em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.3em;font-size:10pt;" height="16.6" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 12.45)" width="455.38"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A10.p1.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:32.91em;">
<span id="A10.p1.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A10.p1.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:120%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">LLM Generator Prompt (Computation)</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 19.16 18.85)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:44.43em;--ltx-fo-height:35.29em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:10pt;" class="ltx_minipage" height="490.76" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 488.3)" width="52.27em"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><pre id="A10.p1.pic1.2" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">You are a professional geometry problem authoring expert, proficient in
Euclidean plane geometry and competition-level geometry problems (such as
AMC / AIME / Math Olympiad).

[Task Objective]

Based on the input &lt;problem&gt; (geometric premises) and conclusion, you need to:
1. Understand the geometric configuration described (points, line segments,
   perpendicular, parallel, equal lengths, similarity, collinearity, etc.).
2. On the basis of this geometric configuration, design a high-quality,
   high-difficulty numerical geometry problem (with only one solving target).
3. Provide a complete problem statement, detailed reasoning process (CoT),
   and the final numerical answer.

The problem statement should use "geometric language" only, do not use
coordinate systems.

--------------------------------
[Problem Requirements]

1. **Numerical Settings**
   - Set reasonable numerical values for side lengths, angles, ratios, etc.
     (recommended: integers or simple fractions in the range 2-20, e.g.,
     3/2, 5/3).
   - The answer should not be too simple (avoid obvious results like 0, 1, 2;
     avoid cases where the answer is identical to a given quantity).

2. **Solving Target Type (only one)**
   The problem should end with a single solving target, ending with "Find...".
   It can be:
   - The length of a line segment;
   - The degree measure of an angle or its trigonometric value;
   - The ratio of two line segments;
   - The area / perimeter of a triangle or quadrilateral;
   - Angles, arc lengths, areas involving circles;
   - Arithmetic operations on the above quantities (e.g., AB² + AC², area ratios).

3. **Geometric Logic Requirements**
   - The problem must be logically self-consistent, non-contradictory, and
     have a unique solution.
   - Degenerate cases are not allowed (e.g., three collinear points forming
     a triangle).
   - If new points are introduced (e.g., intersection points, foots of
     perpendiculars, midpoints), they must be clearly defined.

4. **Problem Statement Format**
   - Natural language narrative, using LaTeX mathematical notation
     (e.g., AB, angleABC, S_triangleABC).
   - Do not include reasoning content like conclusion, only include
     construction content.
   - The last sentence should end with "Find...".

5. **CoT Reasoning Process**
   - Write in Step1 / Step2 / Step3... format.
   - Use LaTeX mathematical notation and formulas.
   - Do not mention DSL, &lt;problem&gt;, symbolic propositions, etc., only reason
     based on the problem statement.

6. **Answer Format**
   - "answer": Only provide the final numerical value or expression,
     e.g., "15/2", "5sqrt3".
   - Do not include explanatory text.

--------------------------------
[Input Format]

&lt;problem&gt; {problem} &lt;/problem&gt;
&lt;conclusion&gt; {conclusion} &lt;/conclusion&gt;
{aux_section}

[Output Format]

Output only a JSON object:

{
  "question": "(Problem statement using LaTeX math notation)",
  "cot": "Step1 ...\nStep2 ...\nStep3 ...",
  "answer": "(Final numerical result, only provide value or expression)"
}
  
</pre></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<div id="A10.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent ltx_align_center"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A10.p2.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="682.23" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 653.15 682.23" width="653.15"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,682.23) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#CCCCCC;" fill="#CCCCCC" fill-opacity="0.5" stroke-opacity="0.5"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 3.54 3.76 L 3.54 671.38 C 3.54 675.42 6.81 678.69 10.85 678.69 L 649.39 678.69 C 653.42 678.69 656.69 675.42 656.69 671.38 L 656.69 3.76 C 656.69 -0.27 653.42 -3.54 649.39 -3.54 L 10.85 -3.54 C 6.81 -3.54 3.54 -0.27 3.54 3.76 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000099;" fill="#000099" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 5.53 L 0 676.7 C 0 679.75 2.48 682.23 5.53 682.23 L 647.61 682.23 C 650.67 682.23 653.15 679.75 653.15 676.7 L 653.15 5.53 C 653.15 2.48 650.67 0 647.61 0 L 5.53 0 C 2.48 0 0 2.48 0 5.53 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#F7F7FF;" fill="#F7F7FF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.38 5.53 L 1.38 654.98 L 651.77 654.98 L 651.77 5.53 C 651.77 3.24 649.91 1.38 647.61 1.38 L 5.53 1.38 C 3.24 1.38 1.38 3.24 1.38 5.53 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 19.16 664.46)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:32.91em;--ltx-fo-height:0.9em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.3em;font-size:10pt;" height="16.6" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 12.45)" width="455.38"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A10.p2.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:32.91em;">
<span id="A10.p2.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A10.p2.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:120%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">LLM Generator Prompt (Proof)</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 19.16 18.85)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:44.43em;--ltx-fo-height:44.89em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:10pt;" class="ltx_minipage" height="623.59" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 621.13)" width="52.27em"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><pre id="A10.p2.pic1.2" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">You are a professional geometry problem authoring expert, proficient in
Euclidean plane geometry and competition-level geometry problems (such as
AMC / AIME / Math Olympiad).

[Task Objective]

Based on the input &lt;problem&gt; (geometric premises) and &lt;conclusion&gt; (the
conclusion to be proved), you need to:
1. Understand the geometric configuration described (points, line segments,
   perpendicular, parallel, equal lengths, similarity, collinearity, etc.).
2. Convert the symbolic geometric premises and conclusion into a natural
   language geometry proof problem.
3. Provide a complete problem statement, detailed proof process (CoT), and
   proof conclusion.

The problem statement should use "geometric language" only, do not use
coordinate systems.

--------------------------------
[Problem Requirements]

1. **Problem Statement Construction**
   - Convert the premises in &lt;problem&gt; into natural language descriptions.
   - Convert the conclusion in &lt;conclusion&gt; into a natural language proof goal.
   - You may add auxiliary conditions in the problem statement (such as
     midpoints, angle bisectors, division points, etc.), but they must be
     reasonable and compatible with the geometric structure in &lt;problem&gt;.
   - Do not introduce new "unknown quantities" or additional parameters
     (such as new variables x, y, t, k, etc.) in the problem statement and
     proof process. If quantity relationships need to be expressed, use
     known quantities (side lengths, angles, ratios given in the problem)
     or their combinations directly.

2. **Proof Goal**
   - The problem should end with "Prove that..." to clearly state the
     geometric conclusion to be proved.
   - The proof goal can be:
     - Two line segments are equal or proportional;
     - Two angles are equal or proportional;
     - Certain points are collinear or concyclic;
     - Certain lines are parallel or perpendicular;
     - Certain triangles are similar or congruent;
     - Other geometric relationships.

3. **Geometric Logic Requirements**
   - The problem must be logically self-consistent, non-contradictory, and
     provable.
   - Degenerate cases are not allowed (e.g., three collinear points forming
     a triangle).
   - If new points are introduced (e.g., intersection points, foots of
     perpendiculars, midpoints), they must be clearly defined.
   - The premises must be sufficient to derive the conclusion.

4. **Problem Statement Format**
   - Natural language narrative in Chinese, using LaTeX mathematical notation
     (e.g., AB, angleABC, S_triangleABC).
   - Do not include reasoning content like conclusion, only include
     construction content and proof goal.
   - The last sentence should end with "Prove that...".

5. **CoT Proof Process**
   - Write the complete proof process in Step1 / Step2 / Step3... format.
   - Use LaTeX mathematical notation and formulas.
   - Each step should explain the geometric theorem or property used
     (such as congruence, similarity, parallel line properties, circle
     properties, etc.).
   - Do not mention DSL, &lt;problem&gt;, symbolic propositions, etc., only
     perform geometric reasoning based on the problem statement.
   - The proof process should be logically clear and complete.

6. **Answer Format**
   - "answer": Provide the proof conclusion, formatted as "QED" or
     "Therefore, [conclusion]".
   - If the conclusion involves quantity relationships, express the conclusion
     directly using known quantities or their combinations, do not introduce
     additional unknown quantities.

--------------------------------
[Input Format]

&lt;problem&gt; {problem} &lt;/problem&gt;
&lt;conclusion&gt; {conclusion} &lt;/conclusion&gt;
{aux_section}

[Output Format]

Output only a JSON object:

{
  "question": "(Problem statement using LaTeX math notation, ending with
               ’Prove that...’)",
  "cot": "Step1 ...\nStep2 ...\nStep3 ...",
  "answer": "(Proof conclusion, e.g., ’QED’ or ’Therefore, [conclusion]’)"
}
  
</pre></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>

=====================
[Problem Text]
{question}
=====================

Please output a piece of **executable Python code** that strictly satisfies
the following requirements:

=====================================================
[Global Code Constraints]
=====================================================
1. You must generate **complete, executable Python code**, do not output
   explanations, comments, or extra text.
2. All variables, functions, and constants must be explicitly defined or
   imported in the code.
3. All coordinates must be **concrete numerical values (float or int)**,
   do not use symbolic expressions, lambdas, undefined variables, or lazy
   expressions.
4. Standard library imports are allowed (e.g., ‘import math‘, ‘import numpy‘),
   but file I/O and network requests are prohibited.

=====================================================
[Geometric Construction Rules]
=====================================================
1. **Point Name Restrictions**: Only use points mentioned in the problem
   statement, do not introduce any new points.
2. **Geometric Relationship Constraints**: Coordinates must satisfy all
   geometric relationships appearing in the problem statement, for example:
   - Perpendicular, parallel
   - Collinear
   - Midpoint
   - On circle
   - Ratio relationships
   - Equal lengths
   - ...
   Do not add properties not mentioned in the problem (such as isosceles,
   perpendicular, parallel, etc.).
3. **Non-degenerate Figure**:
   - Do not allow two different points to coincide
   - Do not allow three points that should form an angle/triangle to be
     nearly collinear
   - Coordinates should be dispersed and stable
4. Geometric relationships must be guaranteed to hold through explicit
   construction (e.g., through slope, vectors, distance from point to
   circle center, etc.).

=====================================================
[Final Output Structure]
=====================================================
At the end of the code, construct and print the following dictionary. The
dictionary should only contain point coordinates, do not include any other
content (field names must match exactly):

result = {
    "points": {   # Coordinate mapping for all points
        "A": (xA, yA),
        "B": (xB, yB),
        ...
    }
}

import json
print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False))

You must output only Python code, do not include any explanatory text or
non-code content.
